supersedes: modern/spec/pic2d/pic2d-model-v1.1.json (time step, gates and artifact contracts unchanged; this file records the operating point sized from measured kinetics and the resumable steady-state runner)
what_changed: operating point sized from the v2 kinetic loss fraction and ion residence time, not from the 0-D Bohm bound
single-case detached, checkpointed, resumable runner with a continuously evaluated plateau criterion (experiments/pic2d_cft_steady_state_v1)
Simulation.load_state re-bases the interval bookkeeping (cumulative tallies, interval step base, energy/electrode samples) so a resumed session reports correct interval currents

kinetic_sizing.source: modern/experiments/pic2d_cft_snapshot_v2/results/fine-w6e4 (cross-check fine-w3e4), 30-sample (9 ns) running means of the 200-step series

loss_fraction_f_L_over_S.reading: f is flat, not approaching 1: source and loss both scale with the plasma inventory

tau_i_eff_s.definition: N_i / L (ions per unit ion loss rate); it saturates at 2.4 us once the first ions born at t = 0 have reached the boundaries, i.e. this IS the kinetic ion residence time (the Bohm/free-fall estimate used in v2 was 1.0 us)

measured_at_n_g_1e20_3ma.nu_iz_definition: S / N_e, ionisations per plasma electron per second (includes the beam contribution, so it is an upper estimate of the plasma-electron rate); <sigma v>_eff = nu_iz / n_g = 1.2e-14 m^3/s at the density-weighted <T_e> = 6.4 eV
measured_at_n_g_1e20_3ma.growth: dN_i/dt = S - L = (nu_iz - 1/tau) N: predicted 8e5 s^-1, observed exponential growth of N_i over the trailing half 9.0e5 s^-1 (e-folding 1.1 us) in both fine cases - the v2 plateau failure was a genuine avalanche (nu_iz tau > 1), not a transient
measured_at_n_g_1e20_3ma.beam_definition: S - nu_iz N_e before the avalanche (t = 0.25 us): ~2.7 ionisations per injected 300 V electron; scales as n_g x I_inj

equilibrium_model.equation: N_eq = a tau / (1 - nu_iz tau), a = beam-driven ionisation rate (prop. to n_g I_inj), nu_iz prop. to n_g at fixed T_e, tau = 2.4 us assumed unchanged (set by the 300 V potential structure)
equilibrium_model.at_5e19: nu_iz tau = 1.45: still runaway unless T_e falls by ~30 % - the user's 5e19 mark is not a plausible plateau point with static neutrals
equilibrium_model.sensitivity: at n_g = 1.5e19, 3 mA: n_eq = 9.3e16 (rate coefficient as measured), 1.5e17 (1.5x, hotter electrons at lower collisionality), 4.2e17 (2x); the fail-closed gate at 5.6e18 node density covers the remaining uncertainty
equilibrium_model.approach_time_constant_s: tau / (1 - nu_iz tau) = 4.3 us at 1.5e19 (5.7 us at 2e19); the 5 % / trailing-20 % plateau rule fires at ~2.8 time constants for an exponential approach

operating_point_v1_2.regime: sub-critical, beam-sustained discharge (nu_iz tau = 0.44 at the measured rate): the plasma density is set by the injected current, not by an ionisation-loss balance; a real CFT at 0.1-1 A and n_g ~ 1e20-1e21 is super-critical and self-limits through neutral depletion and T_e, neither of which is modelled here
operating_point_v1_2.why_below_the_5e19_mark: n_g >= 3.4e19 has no static-neutral equilibrium at the observed T_e; 1.5e19 leaves a 2.3x margin on the rate coefficient and a 4.3 us approach time so the plateau is reachable inside the 12 h wall budget

resolution_budget_v1_2.expected_plateau: ~2.8 x 4.3 us = 12 us = 8.0e6 steps; at 2-3 ms/step 4.5-6.7 h

steady_state_runner.checkpoint: checkpoint/checkpoint-latest.{json,npz} rewritten by directory swap (tmp -> live, old kept until the swap completes) after every <= 40000-step chunk; resume loads it (hash-bound to config, field, cross sections, code identity) and continues bitwise
steady_state_runner.status: status.jsonl: one line per 200-step sync with step, time_s, electrons, ions, discharge_a, exit_ion_beam_a, n_e_peak_node_per_m3 (from the peak omega_pe dt), n_e_mean_per_m3, t_e_mean_ev, omega_pe_dt_max, phi_max_v, wall_seconds_total (cumulative over sessions), ms_per_step, latest plateau evaluation; 'event' lines mark resume/stop
steady_state_runner.series: series.jsonl holds the full SeriesRecord per sync and is truncated to the checkpoint step on resume; series.npz is rebuilt from it at the stop
steady_state_runner.plateau: linear fit over the trailing plateau_window_fraction (0.2) of the elapsed simulated time for I_d and N_e; drift = slope x window / |mean| < 0.05 for both, and >= 3 ion transit times (2.4 us each) elapsed; evaluated after every chunk
steady_state_runner.on_stop: summary.json, series.npz, maps.npz (last completed 400000-step window, or the current one if >= half full), checkpoint-final.*; exit 0
steady_state_runner.resume_caveat: the interval ledger restarts at the resume step: the first record of a session has zero interval residual and electrode work, and the map window restarts

tests: tests/pic2d/test_pic2d_steady_state_runner.py: plateau needs both drifts and 3 transits; exponential approach declared at 3.0-4.6 tau; ramp never, noisy constant yes; one status line and series record per sync; checkpoint per chunk; summary on stop; interrupted+resumed run equals the uninterrupted run bitwise (checkpoint-final arrays, counts, interval currents) with a stray post-checkpoint record dropped; Simulation.load_state re-bases the interval bookkeeping
unchanged_simplifications: static uniform neutral background (at 1.5e19 and S ~ 1.3e16 s^-1 the depletion is ~0.25 % per us; ~3 % over a 12 us run)
no ion-neutral elastic or charge-exchange collisions
no secondary emission; Dirichlet exit plane; prescribed B; electrostatic; momentum-conserving scheme; ions every 8 steps
